LESSON: WRITING 10.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING: THANK YOU AND CONGRATULATORY NOTES

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.5: Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How are strong emotions expressed in writing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise the key elements and layout of a thank you and a congratulatory note
2. use the correct format to write a thank you note
3. write a congratulatory note correctly

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 10.5.1 Functional Writing: Thank you and Congratulatory notes makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. List some of the ocassions when we write a thank you and a congratulatory note,
2. Search for samples of a thank you and a congratulatory note from the internet, newspapers, magazines and textbooks and read through them,
3. Download a thank you and a congratulatory note from the internet and read through them,
4. Self-efficacy: It is developed as the learner successsfully creates congratulatory and thank you notes individually or in small groups
5. Life Skills education (effective communication): It is developed as the learner creates congratulatory and thank you notes and look for artistc ways to make them presentable.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are strong emotions expressed in writing?
2. Why should one write how they feel about something?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
